summary: The plan template that Emil Kowalski's improve-animations skill uses for every animation fix it hands off. Each plan is written for an executor that may be a less capable model with no context and no taste, so it must spell out the problem with file:line citations and verbatim current code, the exact target values, the repo's own conventions with an exemplar, one concrete edit per step, hard scope boundaries, and a verification section that includes a slow-motion feel check. For a design system team it is a ready format for turning motion findings into safe, reviewable work that cheaper agents or junior contributors can carry out without guessing.
key_ideas: Write plans for the weakest executor: zero context, zero taste.
Never point back to earlier discussion; inline every value, path and code excerpt.
Stamp each plan with the commit it was written against so drift can be detected.
Problem sections cite file:line and quote the current code verbatim.
Target sections spell out every curve, duration, spring config and media query.
Plans extend the repo's existing tokens and patterns, shown through one exemplar.
Boundaries limit edits to motion properties, forbid new dependencies, and require stopping on drift.
Verification pairs mechanical checks with a feel check in slow motion and under reduced motion.
One plan per finding, merged only when files and fix pattern are identical.
A plans/README.md index tracks order, dependencies and status.

rules.rule: Write every animation-fix plan in the fixed structure: a title line '# NNN — <Short imperative title>' followed by Status, Commit, Severity, Category and Estimated scope, then Problem, Target, Repo conventions to follow, Steps, Boundaries and Verification sections.
rules.why: Every plan written by improve-animations follows this structure.
rules.evidence: Every plan written by improve-animations follows this structure

rules.rule: Write the plan so an executor with zero context and zero taste can complete it; the plan must contain everything, exactly.
rules.why: The executor may be a less capable model.
rules.evidence: the plan must contain everything, exactly

rules.rule: Never refer back to earlier discussion such as 'the audit above' or 'the easing we discussed'.
rules.why: The executor has no context from that discussion.
rules.evidence: No references to "the audit above" or "the easing we discussed."

rules.rule: Set a new plan's Status to TODO.
rules.why: Template header field.

rules.rule: Stamp the Commit field with the output of git rev-parse --short HEAD at the time the plan is written.
rules.why: Lets the executor detect drift since the commit stamp.

rules.rule: Mark Severity as exactly one of HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW, and name the audit category.
rules.why: Template header fields.

rules.rule: State the estimated scope as the number of files and a rough size.
rules.why: Template header field.

rules.rule: In Problem, say what is wrong, where, and why it matters to how the product feels.
rules.why: Template Problem section.

rules.rule: Cite every problem location as path/to/file.tsx:123 and include the current code verbatim.
rules.why: Template Problem section.

rules.rule: Label each code excerpt with a comment giving its location and whether it is the current or the target code, e.g. /* src/components/dropdown.css:14 — current */ and /* target */.
rules.why: The template's Problem and Target excerpts are labelled this way.

rules.rule: In Target, spell out the exact end state with every value: curves, durations, spring configs and media queries.
rules.why: The executor has zero context and zero taste, so the plan must contain everything, exactly.

rules.rule: Never write a vague target such as 'use a nicer easing'.
rules.why: Every value must be spelled out.

rules.rule: Document how the codebase already handles the pattern (token names, file placement, prop patterns) and give one exemplar file:line for the executor to imitate.
rules.why: The executor should follow repo conventions.
values: <exemplar file:line that already does this correctly>

rules.rule: Add new easing curves to the repo's existing token file rather than inline, e.g. --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) in src/styles/tokens.css.
rules.why: Template example of following repo conventions.

rules.rule: Write Steps as one concrete edit per step: the file, what changes, and the resulting code.
rules.why: Template Steps section.

rules.rule: List the files and components the executor must not touch.
rules.why: Template Boundaries section.
rules.evidence: Do NOT touch <files/components out of scope>

rules.rule: Restrict the executor to motion properties; do not change markup or structure unless a step says so.
rules.why: Template Boundaries section.
rules.evidence: Do NOT change markup/structure — motion properties only

rules.rule: Do not add new dependencies in an animation-fix plan.
rules.why: Template Boundaries section.

rules.rule: If a step does not match the code found (drift since the commit stamp), stop and report instead of improvising.
rules.why: Template Boundaries section.
rules.evidence: STOP and report instead of improvising

rules.rule: In Verification, give the exact mechanical commands (typecheck, lint, build) with their expected outcome.
rules.why: Template Verification section.

rules.rule: Include a feel check: run the UI, trigger the interaction, and list observable checks such as 'the dropdown scales from its trigger, not from center' and 'spamming the toggle never restarts the animation from zero'.
rules.why: Motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong.

rules.rule: In the feel check, set DevTools animation playback to 10% (Animations panel) and confirm the specific detail.
rules.why: Motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong; the executor needs concrete things to watch for in slow motion.
rules.evidence: In DevTools, set playback to 10% (Animations panel)

rules.rule: In the feel check, toggle prefers-reduced-motion (Rendering panel) and confirm movement is dropped but opacity feedback remains.
rules.why: Template verification step for reduced motion.

rules.rule: End Verification with 'Done when' criteria that a machine or an eye can check.
rules.why: Template Verification section.

rules.rule: Write one plan per finding; merge two findings into one plan only when they share every file and the same fix pattern.
rules.why: Notes for the plan author, e.g. the same easing token swap across components.

rules.rule: Pull every value from AUDIT.md; never approximate from memory.
rules.why: Notes for the plan author.

rules.rule: Never skip the feel check; give the executor or reviewer concrete things to watch in slow motion.
rules.why: Motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong.
rules.evidence: The feel check is not optional.

rules.rule: After writing plans, create or update plans/README.md with a table of plans (number, title, severity, status), the recommended execution order and dependencies between plans.
rules.why: Notes for the plan author.

decisions.question: Should related animation findings be fixed in one plan or several?

options.name: One plan per finding
options.effect: Each fix is small, reviewable and independently executable.

options.name: Merged plan
options.effect: One plan covers several findings with the same edit.
options.when: Only when the findings share every file and the same fix pattern, such as the same easing token swap across components.

decisions.recommendation: One plan per finding; merge only when files and fix pattern are identical.

process.detail: Title '# NNN — <Short imperative title>', then Status TODO, Commit from git rev-parse --short HEAD, Severity HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, audit Category, and Estimated scope (files, rough size).
What is wrong, where, and why it matters to how the product feels; cite every location as file:line and quote current code verbatim.
The exact end state with every curve, duration, spring config and media query spelled out, pulled from AUDIT.md.
Where tokens live, naming, file placement and prop patterns, plus one exemplar file:line to imitate.
Numbered steps, each one concrete edit with the file, the change and the resulting code.
Out-of-scope files, motion properties only, no new dependencies, stop and report on drift.
Mechanical commands with expected outcome; a feel check with observable checks, 10% playback in DevTools and a reduced-motion toggle; Done-when criteria.
Create or update plans/README.md with the plan table (number, title, severity, status), execution order and dependencies.

caveats: This is an AI-agent skill file pinned to commit 85e8e23 of emilkowalski/skills.
The file paths (src/styles/tokens.css, src/components/dropdown.css:14) are placeholders in a template, not real files.
The DevTools panel names (Animations, Rendering) are written without naming a browser.

The template governs plan documents for code changes; its only motion values are in the example (the --ease-out curve and a 200ms dropdown transition), which agree with AUDIT.md's --ease-out token and 150–250ms dropdown band [inferred].
